title: The butcher who taught a brahmin
hookLine: an angry sage, a busy housewife, and a butcher who teaches dharma
carry: sadharana dharma: one floor under everyone
tomorrow: a week inside a hard book. what's the one move worth keeping?

cards: A young brahmin named Kaushika sits under a tree reciting the Veda. A crane in the branches soils him. He glares up in anger, and the bird falls dead.
Shaken, he goes begging for food. At one door, a housewife asks him to wait while she serves her husband first. When she finally comes, he's furious.
She answers calmly: I'm no crane.

teach.b: She sends him to Mithila, to learn dharma from a meat-seller there. Kaushika finds the man in the market, and the butcher greets him: I know the housewife sent you.
Then the butcher teaches the proud brahmin: truth, self-control, doing one's own work honestly, caring for his old parents. The Mahabharata gives the lesson to a butcher, and the brahmin learns.
That's a real Hindu idea with a name, sadharana dharma, the dharma common to all.

teach.h: DHARMA IN BRIEF, FOR ALL FOUR.
teach.b: The Manusmriti, after long passages on duties that differ by varna, gives it in one line: not harming, truthfulness, not stealing, purity, restraint of the senses; this, Manu says, is dharma in brief for all four varnas.
Ahimsa, satyam, asteyam. A neighbor tradition says something close.

In the Torah, God tells Moses to speak to all the congregation of Israel, and a long list follows, including, in the JPS translation: "Ye shall not steal; neither shall ye deal falsely, nor lie one to another."

Shared: two old law codes that lay a short floor under a whole people. An honest difference: Leviticus gives the reason, be holy, for God is holy; Manu's floor sits beside duties that still differ by birth.
Neither is ranked here. Both put a floor where everyone stands.

how: Hindu teachers call the duties shared by everyone sadharana dharma and often cite Manusmriti 10.63's short list (ahimsa, truth, not stealing, purity, restraint); the story of Kaushika and the righteous butcher of Mithila is retold from the Mahabharata's forest book. Jewish communities read Leviticus 19 in the yearly Torah cycle.

o: a book of rules for monks who leave home
a list of the fasts kept during a festival
an old law book with one short dharma for all

games.q: the floor for everyone — tap the pairs.
p: ye shall not steal, nor lie

s: the Manusmriti has no rule that applies to everyone the same
10.63 gives a short dharma for all four varnas: not harming, truth, not stealing, purity, restraint.
in the Mahabharata, a meat-seller teaches dharma to a brahmin
the housewife sends Kaushika to the butcher of Mithila, and he learns.
in Leviticus, the list is given to all the congregation of Israel
God tells Moses to speak to all the congregation; the list includes no stealing and no lying.

games.q: at a family puja, a cousin says Hindu dharma is different for every caste, so there's nothing everyone shares. what does today's lesson answer?
o: there's sadharana dharma: no harm, truth, no stealing, purity, restraint, for all.
he's right; every duty in the old books depends on birth.
dharma only means the rituals each family does at home.
games.why: Manu gives dharma in brief for all four varnas, and the Mahabharata lets a butcher teach a brahmin. a floor sits under everyone.

practice: Count, on the fingers of one hand, five people who kept that floor with you: someone who told you the truth, someone who didn't take what was yours, someone who could have hurt you and didn't.
One finger and one slow breath for each. If you pray, you can give thanks for them.

wordCard.voice: The Manusmriti: a book of rules that differ by birth, with one short dharma for all: ahimsa, truth, not stealing, purity, restraint.

orig.note: Sanskrit, Manusmriti 10.63: not harming, truth, not stealing, the first three of the five.

carryVoice: Your line: sadharana dharma, one floor under everyone, and a butcher can teach it to a brahmin. More tomorrow.
